column10: STATUS CO was built from nothing, entirely through digital means, and every part of it had to sit under one language. The website carries that logic. The first drop lives on the site as a spatial copy of the pop-up itself: every object modelled in 3D at true scale, optimised for the web, placed exactly where it stood. Visitors who came to the event can walk the room again and catch the details they missed standing in it. Click an object and it opens its photographs, its specs, the thinking behind it. The site introduces the brand and runs as a live digital twin of the space at the same time.

column10: Edetri is a tableware brand working mainly in glass and ceramic, gathering its community around events built on those products. Ahead of a new line in metal and glass, the identity was studied for where it could go next: graphically, in language, and in attitude. The outcome was a board built specifically for the brand, carrying annotation and comment tools so both sides could mark what worked and what did not, and settle the direction together.

column10: Following the brand strategy work on the board and the study of Edetri's new era, every product and every event was re-visualised under one language and gathered into a booklet. Edetri had been known through its products, and the aim here was to balance that weight editorially by giving the events equal ground. The graphic language comes out of the way metal and glass meet in the new collection, and it marks the first step of the new era: digital and romantic, stripped back and poetic, industrial and felt.
column16: Every Edetri product and event re-visualised under one language in a booklet, balancing the brand's product reputation with editorial weight in a register that is digital and romantic, stripped back and poetic, industrial and felt.
